title: OSINT Fundamentals & Browser Setup
description: Learn what OSINT is, prepare your system, and configure Firefox for privacy-focused investigations.

sections.title: What is OSINT?
sections.description: OSINT stands for Open-Source Intelligence. It involves collecting, analyzing, and connecting information from publicly available sources. It is a huge field within cybersecurity.
sections.note: Privacy is one of the most important principles in OSINT. If your own device is leaking information, your investigation can expose your identity.

sections.title: System Preparation
sections.description: Before starting any OSINT investigation, prepare your system with basic security tools.

tools.name: ClamAV
tools.description: Open-source antivirus engine. Scan files and directories for known malware — useful when downloading files from untrusted sources. Install via: sudo apt install clamav

commands.description: Update system package information to get latest available software versions.
Install ClamAV antivirus engine on your Linux system.
Scan a specific file for malware. Replace <file-path> with actual file location.
Example: scan a PDF file called example.pdf in current directory.

sections.title: Firefox Privacy Extensions
sections.description: Install these extensions to block trackers, ads, and malicious scripts before they interact with your browser.

tools.name: uBlock Origin
tools.description: Powerful open-source content blocker. Blocks advertisements, trackers, and unwanted network requests.

tools.name: Privacy Badger
tools.description: Detects and blocks third-party trackers that attempt to follow you across different websites.

tools.name: NoScript
tools.description: Controls which websites can execute JavaScript. Blocks unwanted scripts from malicious or compromised sites. Note: may break some legitimate websites.

sections.title: Firefox Privacy Settings
sections.description: Configure Firefox built-in privacy settings. Go to Menu → Settings → Privacy & Security.
topics: Disable Firefox Data Collection and Use (telemetry)

commands.description: Open Firefox advanced configuration. Type this in the address bar and press Enter.

sections.title: about:config Privacy Settings
sections.description: Advanced Firefox settings to minimize browser fingerprinting and data leakage during OSINT investigations.

commands.description: Enables Firefox built-in tracking protection. Blocks known tracking resources and scripts.
Disables geolocation API. Websites cannot use Firefox to request your device location.
Disables built-in phishing protection. Trade-off: be extra careful about websites you visit.
Limits websites ability to receive clipboard events when copying or pasting content.
Prevents websites from discovering available microphones and cameras on your device.
Disables Battery Status API. Removes battery info as a browser fingerprinting data point.

sections.title: WebRTC — Most Important
sections.description: WebRTC enables real-time audio/video in browsers but can leak your real IP address even when using a VPN. Disable it for OSINT work.
sections.note: Disabling WebRTC will break browser-based video/voice calls. Only disable during investigations.

commands.description: Disables WebRTC peer connection. Prevents potential IP leakage outside VPN tunnel.
Disables TURN server usage in WebRTC connections.
Prevents use of document-specified ICE servers in WebRTC.
Disables WebRTC video peer connections completely.
